title: About WoWSP
subtitle: World of WarShip Panel
description: A desktop dashboard for World of Warships: standalone replay review with a holographic 3D map, plus an in-game transparent overlay for live stats lookup.
trivia01: Yukikaze's torpedoes reach just 8 km, yet each carries 21,367 alpha at 76 knots — the same Type F3 hardware as Shimakaze's, on a much faster reload.
trivia02: Mash the M key twice: during the tactical-map camera transition the view briefly lifts high enough to aim at enemies hiding behind islands.
trivia03: Near the end of Operation Raptor Rescue, a little paper-folded ship sometimes drifts outside the map border: shells cannot touch it, only ship-launched torpedoes can — and a hit unlocks the hidden 「Insert Coin」 achievement.
trivia04: Yamato's 460 mm guns play the overmatch rule: once the caliber exceeds 14.3 times the plate thickness, the armor can no longer ricochet the shell — but overmatch is not a guaranteed penetration; if the shell has lost too much penetration at range, it still fails to punch through.
trivia05: Radar spots ships straight through islands and smoke, and hydroacoustic search does the same when hunting surface ships; only submarine detection is blocked by islands. Do not lump「hydro」and「submarine surveillance」together. On the Lesta server, radar and hydro may not see through islands at all.
trivia06: The hardest-hitting torpedo in the game does not belong to a destroyer but to British battleships: the 622 mm Mk I at 29,367 alpha, carried by Rodney, Duncan and St. Vincent.
trivia07: Kitakami and her 40 torpedo tubes were once judged too toxic for the game: pulled in 2015, she only returned eight years later (December 2023) as a Tier X cruiser.
trivia08: Shimakaze's 20 km torpedoes are nicknamed the 「wall of skill」: 62 knots slow and spotted from 2.5 km, dodgeable by anyone — the name is pure sarcasm.
trivia09: Magazine detonations haunted players for over eight years until they were removed outright in December 2024 (Update 13.11), retiring the legendary Juliet Charlie 「no-detonation」 flag along the way.
trivia10: Shell damage math: over-pens pay 10%, penetrations 33%, citadel hits 100% — and destroyers have no citadel at all, so AP of 280 mm or larger is capped at 10% against them.
trivia11: Operation Killer Whale can spawn a friendly bot Farragut commanded by Commander Jenkins: keep him alive until victory and you earn the one-time hidden 「Save Commander Jenkins」 achievement.
trivia12: The biggest guns in the game sit on Satsuma: four twin 510 mm mounts on a 35-second reload, based on the real IJN 「Super Yamato」 design study.
trivia13: Actually, it is this pig talking to you right now. Probably.
trivia14: Wowo-nyan (窝窝娘), the official VTuber of the Chinese server, is actually based on a catshark — not on the Schlieffen.
trivia15: These fun facts were hand-picked by the pig itself, which refuses to take any responsibility for their accuracy.
trivia16: Different shell types on the same gun can have different maximum ranges: Yamato's AP falls short of her HE — shell weight and ballistics differ, so not every shell actually flies out to the theoretical maximum range.
trivia17: In Operations and event modes, hydroacoustic search can even「hear」coastal bunkers — though most players suspect this is a bug rather than a design choice.
trivia18: Black's torpedoes have a higher guaranteed damage floor than her peers, so even a glancing hit still hurts.
trivia19: Pan-European destroyers already carry quadruple torpedo tubes at Tier III — small hulls, lavish launchers.
trivia20: Edinburgh's in-game model really does hide gold: she went down carrying Soviet gold in 1942, and the model keeps the Easter egg.
trivia21: Special ships like Lobster-Eyed are actually repurposed big-head (chibi) models — give one a new skin and it becomes a brand-new ship.
trivia22: Quackaducko stows her mines inside the X turret position at the stern; incidentally, mines are currently a Lesta-server-only weapon.
trivia23: Valparaíso can carry up to seven Repair Parties — a floating hospital, and then some.
trivia24: The WG server briefly had Vyazma and Oregon: burst fire from a limited stock of special shells, plus excellent penetration, made them a force in Ranked for a while; but WG knew full well they were too unbalanced and never intended them to stay.
trivia25: WG once released a video promising submarines would never be added — well, you know how that turned out.
trivia26: The first radar destroyer was Grozovoi — she had radar back when it was still far from standard equipment on destroyers.
trivia27: Jets have been in World of Warships for ages, yet not one of the old jet aircraft has ever been sent back for a model rework.
trivia28: Aircraft carriers used to exist at odd tiers: the early CV line spanned tiers 4 to 10, with carriers at 5, 7 and 9 before the rework standardized them on even tiers.
trivia29: Japanese heavy cruisers follow a counter-intuitive rule: the higher the tier, the thinner the deck armor.
trivia30: In the earliest version, the French heavy cruiser line was the most expensive grind in the game — consumables cost credits back then, and French heavies carried a lot of them.
trivia31: The original Buffalo had torpedoes — today she is guns only.
trivia32: Among Hipper-class ships, the best concealment belongs to the lowest-tier one: Weser — small ship, easy to hide.
trivia33: Myōkō has more clones than any other silver ship — reskins, premium editions and event versions together could man a whole fleet.
trivia34: WG produced a full How it Works video series; if you have fewer than 1,000 battles, go watch them — that is your homework.
trivia35: Weser's aircraft are the fastest biplanes in the game — faster than Midway's planes.
trivia36: Remember to upgrade Clemson's hull: her main guns turn from single mounts into twins, doubling her firepower.
trivia37: North Carolina's gold camo, stock hull and fully-upgraded hull look like three completely different ships.
trivia38: WoWSP was almost entirely written by Chinese large language models, mainly the DeepSeek and GLM series.
trivia39: Fusō's HE has the longest shell flight time in the game at a ship's natural maximum range: a full 18.3 seconds from muzzle to impact.
trivia40: World of Warships is developed by Lesta and published by WG; after the Russia-Ukraine war split Belarus-based WG and Russia-based Lesta, Lesta began operating its own servers independently.
trivia41: In the Soviet battleship line, only Tier IV Gangut is a genuinely completed historical ship; Tier IX Sovetsky Soyuz barely counts (laid down but never finished), and Novorossiysk is historical too — she was the Italian Giulio Cesare, handed over as war reparations. The rest are all paper designs.
trivia42: During World War II the US launched dozens of Essex-class carriers at dumpling-making speed — in China the class is nicknamed「Dumpling-class」.
trivia43: In one battle, @BestNaomi was sailing Vermont when an enemy Ohio one-salvoed him for 83,079 damage — since then, 「83079」 has become an inside joke among Chinese World of Warships players.
trivia44: Some ships have their own unique horn sounds — press N in port or in battle to sound the horn.
